old.H2-P3: The inner pl/ork can start right where you live, though. [Peer counseling](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/p/hearthwork-an-integrated-peer-counseling) only requires two people and a place to talk privately. Reparenting, somatic work, working on jealousy, learning how to repair conflict, etc etc? None of that has to wait for a deed!
old.H2-P4: Even if a group practices together every week for two years, it may never own land. So what? It can still make a difference in how people get through divorce, illness, grief, parenting and plain old loneliness.
old.H3-P5: Have you ever been to an actual community? If not, you should go! [Twin Oaks](https://twinoaks.org/), [East Wind](http://eastwind.org/), [Acorn](https://www.ic.org/directory/acorn-community-farm/) and other [intentional communities](https://www.ic.org/) take visitors, and so do a lot of [ecovillages](https://ecovillage.org/) (just check their current visitor requirements before you go).
old.H3-P6: What will you learn from a visit? Things no manifesto can tell you. How much togetherness you actually enjoy, for one, and what kind of privacy you need. And which labor system drives you bananas! And whether communal showers feel liberating, or send you off pricing studio apartments.
old.H3-P7: What about the land? Do those three things first, before you spend serious time or money looking for it.
old.H3-P8: I'm not trying to sell you a retreat or get you to fill out an application or anything, the manuals I mentioned are free. I've just noticed that community tends to gather wherever people find real care, play, usefulness and room to become more honest.
